sources.entry: Backdrop CMS - Comprehensive CMS for small to medium sized businesses and non-profits. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: Backdrop is a GPL-2.0 content management system for building websites such as blogs, galleries, intranets and business sites, forked from Drupal and aimed at non-technical users.
summary.what_it_does: Backdrop is a full-featured CMS that lets non-technical users manage many kinds of content. The README says it can be used for blogs, image galleries, social networks, intranets and similar sites. It states goals of working out-of-the-box, having code that is quick to learn, and offering extensible APIs. It is described as a fork of Drupal that keeps the developer audience focused on ease of use and speed of learning over architectural flexibility. The README covers a browser-based installer that runs after the user creates a MySQL database. Documentation is pointed to the Backdrop Handbook (user guide) and the Backdrop API documentation (developers). Bug reports go to a separate issue tracker, and security issues go to a private security team address.
use_cases: run a photo or image gallery site
create a small business or non-profit website
how_to_run: Create a new MySQL database, username and password for Backdrop
Point your browser at the Backdrop installation URL
Follow the instructions provided by the installer
notable: Forked from Drupal, aiming for ease of use and fast learning
Designed to work out-of-the-box for non-technical users
Documentation provided through the Backdrop Handbook and API docs
caveats: Requires PHP 7.1+ and MySQL 5.5+ with PDO; README recommends a currently supported PHP version
Bug reports are filed in a separate issue tracker outside the main code repository
